analysis.session_summary: The overnight tape was a risk-off grind: CHF led at +0.356% and JPY gained +0.136%, while AUD fell -0.371% and NZD fell -0.398%. USD went nowhere as UoM and Trump remarks were muted; GBP got a clean lift from a 0.7% m/m retail sales beat vs 0.0% forecast. Most major legs had no identifiable news catalyst, leaving flows and technicals in control. VIX rose 6.167%, reinforcing the safe-haven bid.

themes.evidence: GBP +0.121% after Retail Sales m/m came in 0.7% vs 0.0% forecast.
USD strength -0.0% with UoM 51.5 vs 51.7 and Trump speech both muted.

currency_drivers.USD: No own catalyst; UoM and Trump speeches were muted, leaving the dollar flat.
currency_drivers.EUR: No decisive own catalyst; Lagarde was a non-event and euro closed at its session high.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own release; early safe-haven bid faded by 65%, leaving only modest strength.
currency_drivers.GBP: Supported by 0.7% m/m retail sales beat versus 0.0% forecast, keeping sterling near highs.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own data; risk-off sentiment dragged it lower before a 61% retracement.
currency_drivers.CAD: No Canadian catalyst; held a narrow range with no event to move it.
currency_drivers.CHF: No domestic catalyst; safe-haven flow drove strength as VIX rose 6.167%.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own catalyst; risk-off left it weaker after an early gain was 86% retraced.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through alternating up/down legs with only the UoM dip providing a clear USD bid, closing near its session high.

polarity_reads.read: The USD basket was flat despite a slight miss, implying no fresh dollar-down positioning from soft US data.
USD barely moved, but AUD/USD and NZD/USD fell hard on his remarks; risk proxies were the levered short.
The clean GBP beat moved sterling only 0.066%, indicating the market was not heavily short GBP.
A muted EUR reaction shows no new policy signal and no hawkish/dovish repricing.

scenarios.name: Risk-off consolidates
scenarios.thesis: Flash PMIs come in soft but not recessionary; the safe-haven bid in CHF/JPY persists but fresh selling is limited after the overnight move.
triggers: US flash services PMI below 55.6 forecast
scenarios.invalidation: A clean beat in European PMIs and a firm US services print revive risk appetite and unwind CHF.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR lacks own driver but USD flat-to-softer if US PMIs slip from prior highs.
CHF remains the region's safe-haven outperformer while risk sentiment is fragile.

scenarios.name: US PMI disappointment
scenarios.thesis: US flash PMIs undershoot, reinforcing the theme that US exceptionalism is fading; the dollar weakens against high-beta and European FX.
triggers: US Flash Manufacturing PMI below 54.5 forecast
US Flash Services PMI below 55.6 forecast
Fed speakers sound dovish on growth
scenarios.invalidation: US PMIs beat and headline risk appetite returns; dollar squeezes higher.

pair_paths.rationale: A softer US PMI path would give the euro room to extend toward range highs.
Sterling already has a domestic tailwind from retail sales and benefits from dollar weakness.
A lower dollar and stabilising risk sentiment could lift the beaten-down Aussie.

scenarios.name: Risk-off extension
scenarios.thesis: PMIs disappoint across Europe and the US, reinforcing recession fears; risk currencies slide further and safe havens extend gains.
triggers: US services PMI falls more than expected
scenarios.invalidation: Any geopolitical de-escalation or strong PMI beat reverses the safe-haven bid.

pair_paths.rationale: Aussie is the most exposed to global growth and risk sentiment; further weakness likely.
Kiwi has tracked risk-off and remains fragile after Friday's drop.
CHF strengthens in a risk-off shock even as the dollar is mixed.

risks.why_it_matters: They produced sharp reversals in AUD/USD, NZD/USD and oil/gold despite muted USD.
risks.watch: Trump statements and Iran diplomacy headlines

risks.why_it_matters: Flash PMIs can reframe growth and rate expectations quickly for EUR, GBP, USD.
Weekend/Asia tape can exaggerate flow-driven swings and retracements.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Coming window centers on flash PMIs from France, Germany, UK and the US. Soft prints would extend the risk-off, safe-haven bid; firm prints could unwind CHF/JPY strength and lift AUD/NZD.
